name: Propulsion system
description: A propulsion system is a machine that produces thrust to move an object forward.

name: Airbreathing engine
description: An airbreathing engine utilizes the oxygen in the atmospheric air to burn the fuel carried within the vehicle.

name: Non-airbreathing engine
description: A non-airbreathing engine carries both the fuel and the oxidizer required for combustion.

name: Gas generator
description: The core of any gas turbine engine is the gas generator.

name: Turbine
description: The turbine extracts energy from the hot gas to drive the compressor.

name: Turbojet engine
description: A turbojet engine is formed by adding an inlet and an exhaust nozzle to the gas generator.

name: Turbofan engine
description: A turbofan engine adds a fan driven by an additional turbine stage or a separate spool.

name: Turboprop engine
description: A turboprop engine uses a gas turbine core to drive a propeller through a reduction gearbox.

name: Turboshaft engine
description: A turboshaft engine delivers power to a shaft to drive something other than a propeller, such as a helicopter rotor.

name: Ramjet engine
description: The ramjet engine has no moving parts (no compressor or turbine) and relies on forward speed to compress air.

name: Pulsejet engine
description: A pulsejet engine operates with periodic or intermittent combustion using valves or acoustic geometry.

name: Uninstalled thrust
description: The uninstalled thrust (F_n) is the force produced by the engine alone, neglecting installation effects.

name: Installed thrust
description: The installed thrust F is equal to the uninstalled thrust F_n minus the inlet drag D_inlet and the nozzle drag D_nozzle.

name: Inlet drag
description: Drag associated with the engine intake aerodynamic forces.

name: Nozzle drag
description: Drag associated with the exhaust aft-end geometry and flow field.

name: Thrust specific fuel consumption
description: Thrust specific fuel consumption (TSFC or S) is defined as the mass flow rate of fuel divided by the thrust.

name: TSFC
description: Lower TSFC indicates a more fuel-efficient engine for a given thrust requirement.

name: Thermal efficiency
description: Thermal efficiency is the ratio of the rate of kinetic energy production to the thermal power input from fuel.

name: Propulsive efficiency
description: Propulsive efficiency measures how effectively the engine's kinetic energy output is converted into aircraft propulsive power.

name: Overall efficiency
description: The overall efficiency of a propulsion system is the product of its thermal and propulsive efficiencies.

name: Specific thrust
description: Specific thrust is the thrust produced per unit mass flow rate of air entering the engine.

name: Bypass ratio
description: The bypass ratio (alpha) is the ratio of the mass flow rate bypassing the core to the mass flow rate passing through the core.

name: High bypass ratio
description: High bypass ratio engines generally provide lower TSFC at subsonic cruise speeds.

name: Continuity equation
description: The continuity equation expresses the principle of conservation of mass for a control volume.

name: Momentum equation
description: The momentum equation expresses Newton's second law of motion for a fluid passing through a control volume.

name: Energy equation
description: The energy equation is a statement of the first law of thermodynamics applied to a fluid flowing through a control volume.

name: Steady flow
description: A flow is defined as steady if its properties at any point within the control volume do not vary with time.

name: One-dimensional flow
description: A flow is one-dimensional if the fluid properties are uniform across any cross section perpendicular to the flow direction.

name: Perfect gas
description: A perfect gas is a gas whose intermolecular forces are negligible and obeys the thermal equation of state P = rho*R*T.

name: Calorically perfect gas
description: A calorically perfect gas is a perfect gas with constant specific heats (c_p and c_v are constants).

name: Speed of sound
description: The speed of sound 'a' in a calorically perfect gas is given by a = sqrt(gamma * R * T).

name: Mach number
description: The Mach number M is defined as the ratio of the local fluid velocity V to the local speed of sound 'a'.

name: Subsonic flow
description: Flow where the local Mach number is strictly less than 1.0.

name: Supersonic flow
description: Flow where the local Mach number is strictly greater than 1.0.

name: Sonic flow
description: Flow where the local Mach number is exactly equal to 1.0.

name: Stagnation temperature
description: Stagnation temperature (or total temperature) T_t represents the temperature achieved when a fluid is decelerated to zero velocity adiabatically.

name: Stagnation pressure
description: Stagnation pressure (or total pressure) P_t is the pressure attained when a fluid is brought to rest isentropically.

name: Isentropic flow
description: An isentropic flow is both adiabatic and reversible; entropy remains constant along a streamline.

name: Area-Mach number relation
description: The area-Mach number relation links the cross-sectional area of a duct to the local Mach number for an isentropic flow.

name: Convergent duct
description: In a convergent duct, a supersonic flow slows down (Mach number decreases).

name: Divergent duct
description: In a divergent duct, a supersonic flow accelerates (Mach number increases).

name: Throat
description: The location of minimum cross-sectional area is called the throat, where the Mach number can reach unity.

name: Choked flow
description: When the Mach number at the throat reaches unity, the mass flow rate through the nozzle reaches its maximum possible value and is said to be choked.

name: Normal shock
description: A normal shock wave is a thin discontinuity perpendicular to the flow direction that can occur only in supersonic flow.

name: Fanno flow
description: Fanno flow refers to adiabatic flow in a constant-area duct with friction.

name: Rayleigh flow
description: Rayleigh flow refers to frictionless flow in a constant-area duct with heat transfer (heating or cooling).

name: Thermal choking
description: Maximum heat addition in a Rayleigh flow occurs when the Mach number reaches unity; further heating causes thermal choking.

name: Heating in Rayleigh flow
description: Adding heat to a constant-area flow always results in a decrease in total pressure.

name: Rocket engine
description: A rocket engine carries both its fuel and its oxidizer, allowing it to operate in a vacuum outside the atmosphere.

name: Rocket thrust equation
description: The total thrust of a rocket is the sum of the momentum thrust and the pressure thrust: F = m_dot * V_e + (P_e - P_a) * A_e.

name: Momentum thrust
description: The component of thrust generated by the change in momentum of the exhaust gas (m_dot * V_e).

name: Pressure thrust
description: The component of thrust due to the difference between exit pressure and ambient pressure ((P_e - P_a) * A_e).

name: Effective exhaust velocity
description: The effective exhaust velocity C is defined such that F = m_dot * C, which combines momentum and pressure effects.

name: Specific impulse
description: Specific impulse I_sp is the thrust divided by the propellant weight flow rate at sea level: I_sp = F / (m_dot * g_0).

name: Characteristic velocity
description: The characteristic velocity c* is a measure of the combustion chemical energy and efficiency, independent of nozzle characteristics.

name: Thrust coefficient
description: The thrust coefficient C_f measures the amplification of thrust achieved by expanding the gas through the nozzle.

name: Optimum expansion
description: Maximum thrust for a given propellant mass flow and chamber condition occurs when the nozzle exit pressure equals the ambient pressure (P_e = P_a).

name: Overexpanded nozzle
description: A nozzle is overexpanded if the exit pressure is lower than the surrounding ambient atmospheric pressure.

name: Oblique shock
description: When a nozzle is highly overexpanded, oblique shocks or flow separation occur at the nozzle exit.

name: Underexpanded nozzle
description: A nozzle is underexpanded if the gas exits at a pressure higher than the ambient atmospheric pressure.

name: Expansion waves
description: Further expansion takes place outside the nozzle exit through expansion fans when P_e > P_a.

name: Liquid propellant rocket
description: Liquid rocket systems utilize liquid chemical propellants stored in separate tanks.

name: Turbopump feed system
description: High-thrust liquid rockets use turbopumps driven by a gas generator to force propellants into the high-pressure chamber.

name: Pressure-fed system
description: A simpler feed system that uses regulated high-pressure gas to push propellants into the combustion chamber.

name: Solid propellant rocket
description: A solid rocket motor stores its fuel and oxidizer intimately mixed together as a solid block called the grain.

name: Propellant grain
description: Combustion takes place on the internal surfaces of the hollow cavity inside the solid grain.

name: Progressive burning
description: A grain geometry that causes the burning surface area (and therefore thrust) to increase over time.

name: Regressive burning
description: A grain geometry that causes the burning surface area (and therefore thrust) to decrease over time.

name: Neutral burning
description: A grain geometry where the burning surface area remains relatively constant during the burn.

name: Rocket equation
description: The ideal rocket equation (Tsiolkovsky equation) is Delta_V = C * ln(m_i / m_f), neglecting gravity and drag.

name: Initial rocket mass
description: m_i = m_PL + m_s + m_p.

name: Structural coefficient
description: The structural coefficient (epsilon) is the ratio of the structural mass to the sum of the structural and propellant masses.

name: Multistage rocket
description: Multistage rockets discard the dead weight of empty tanks and structures of depleted stages to achieve higher final velocities.

name: Payload ratio
description: The ratio of the carried payload mass to the initial total mass of that specific rocket stage.

name: Parametric cycle analysis
description: The objective of parametric cycle analysis is to relate the engine performance parameters to the design choices and the flight environment.

name: Station numbering
description: The gas turbine industry utilizes standard station numbering (e.g., 0 for ambient, 2 for compressor inlet, 3 for compressor exit, 4 for turbine inlet, 5 for turbine exit, 9 for nozzle exit).

name: Ideal cycle analysis
description: Ideal cycle analysis assumes that the compression and expansion processes are reversible and adiabatic (isentropic).

name: Total temperature ratio tau
description: The dimensionless parameter tau represents the ratio of stagnation temperatures across a component.

name: Total pressure ratio pi
description: The dimensionless parameter pi represents the ratio of stagnation pressures across a component.

name: Isentropic component
description: For ideal isentropic components (compressor or turbine), the total pressure ratio and total temperature ratio are directly coupled.

name: Ideal turbojet
description: For a given maximum turbine inlet temperature, the specific thrust of an ideal turbojet drops to zero at a specific upper flight Mach number limit.

name: Ideal afterburner
description: An afterburner increases the total temperature of the gas entering the exhaust nozzle without affecting the turbomachinery core.

name: Ideal turbofan
description: A turbofan engine divides the incoming air into a primary core stream and a secondary bypass stream.

name: Bypass ratio alpha
description: alpha = m_dot_bypass / m_dot_core.

name: Fan turbine
description: In a turbofan, a low-pressure turbine extracts energy from the core flow to drive the fan.

name: Optimum bypass ratio
description: There exists an mathematically optimum bypass ratio for a given core design that yields the absolute minimum TSFC.

name: Ideal ramjet
description: A ramjet engine has no compressor or turbine; compression is achieved entirely through the dynamic pressure rise in the inlet.

name: Optimal turbofan energy distribution
description: For an unmixed ideal turbofan, the optimum kinetic energy distribution occurs when the exit velocity of the bypass nozzle equals the exit velocity of the core nozzle.

name: Real component performance
description: The performance of real components is characterized by total temperature ratios, total pressure ratios, efficiencies, and pressure losses.

name: Inlet
description: The performance of the inlet (or diffuser) is primarily characterized by its total pressure ratio, pi_d = P_t2 / P_t0, also called the inlet recovery factor.

name: Inlet ram recovery
description: Military specifications (like MIL-E-5007D) define standard inlet recovery curves that decrease as the flight Mach number increases above 1.0.

name: Inlet mass flow ratio
description: The ratio of the actual mass flow entered into the inlet to the maximum possible mass flow that the capture area can intercept.

name: Compressor
description: The isentropic compressor efficiency eta_c is defined as the ratio of ideal (isentropic) work to the actual work required for a given total pressure ratio.

name: Compressor total temperature ratio tau_c
description: tau_c = 1 + (pi_c^((gamma-1)/gamma) - 1) / eta_c, which links actual temperature rise to pressure ratio.

name: Polytropic efficiency
description: Polytropic efficiency (e_c for compressor, e_t for turbine) is defined as the isentropic efficiency of an elemental or infinitesimal stage.

name: Compressor isentropic efficiency
description: For a constant polytropic efficiency e_c, the overall isentropic compressor efficiency eta_c drops as the total pressure ratio pi_c increases due to the preheating effect.

name: Turbine total temperature ratio tau_t
description: tau_t = 1 - eta_t * (1 - pi_t^((gamma-1)/gamma)), which relates the temperature drop to the expansion pressure ratio.

name: Turbine isentropic efficiency
description: For a constant polytropic efficiency e_t, the overall isentropic turbine efficiency eta_t rises as the pressure ratio increases due to the reheating effect.

name: Combustor
description: Combustion efficiency eta_b is the ratio of the actual thermal energy released to the chemical energy available in the fuel.

name: Combustor pressure loss
description: The total pressure ratio of the combustor pi_b = P_t4 / P_t3 is always less than 1.0 due to viscous friction and cold-to-hot flow momentum pressure drop.

name: Afterburner
description: The efficiency eta_AB measures how completely the fuel burns in the afterburner duct upstream of the exit nozzle.

name: Afterburner pressure loss
description: The total pressure ratio pi_AB = P_t7 / P_t6 account for losses due to flameholders, friction, and high-temperature heat addition.

name: Mechanical transmission
description: Mechanical efficiency eta_m accounts for frictional power losses in bearings and accessory gearboxes connecting the turbine and compressor shafts.

name: Exhaust nozzle
description: The exhaust nozzle performance is characterized by its total pressure ratio pi_n = P_t9 / P_t7, which represents friction losses in the nozzle duct.

name: Nozzle angularity coefficient
description: An angularity factor (or divergence factor C_ang) accounts for the non-axial exit velocity vector at the nozzle plane, reducing net thrust.

name: Power take-off
description: Extraction of mechanical shaft power (P_TO) to run aircraft accessories directly reduces the turbine power available to drive the compressor.

name: Bleed air extraction
description: Extracting high-pressure compressed air from the compressor exit for cabin environmental control systems (ECS) or turbine blade cooling reduces the downstream mass flow.

name: Cooling air mixing
description: Reintroducing relatively cool bleed air into the turbine stages for blade cooling causes aerodynamic mixing losses and lowers the effective total temperature of the gas.

name: Real rocket performance
description: Analysis of real rocket engines requires accounting for non-ideal effects including nozzle efficiency, incomplete combustion, heat transfer, and complex chemical behaviors.

name: Combustion chamber pressure
description: Due to high-velocity combustion and friction inside the chamber, the total pressure drops from the injector head to the nozzle throat entrance.

name: Real nozzle expansion
description: Nozzle efficiency eta_n is defined as the ratio of actual kinetic energy change to the ideal isentropic kinetic energy change across the nozzle.

name: Nozzle velocity coefficient
description: The velocity coefficient C_v relates the actual exhaust velocity to the ideal velocity; typically C_v equals the square root of nozzle efficiency.

name: Discharge coefficient
description: The discharge coefficient C_d is the ratio of actual mass flow rate to the ideal isentropic mass flow rate, accounting for boundary layer displacement.

name: Incomplete combustion
description: Failure to achieve perfect chemical equilibrium or full mixing of oxidizer and fuel lowers the combustion temperature T_c below its theoretical adiabatic value.

name: Combustion efficiency
description: Combustion efficiency is often expressed as the ratio of actual characteristic velocity (c*_actual) to the theoretical characteristic velocity (c*_theoretical).

name: Frozen flow
description: Frozen flow assumes that the chemical composition of the exhaust gas remains constant (fixed at chamber exit state) during expansion through the nozzle.

name: Equilibrium flow
description: Equilibrium flow assumes that chemical reactions occur instantaneously as pressure and temperature drop, continually adjusting composition to maintain local equilibrium.

name: Real specific impulse
description: The actual expansion process in a real rocket nozzle falls between the ideal frozen and shifting equilibrium bounds.

name: Thrust chamber heat transfer
description: Heat loss through the chamber walls and nozzle liners directly reduces the thermal energy available for conversion into kinetic energy.

name: Regenerative cooling
description: Regenerative cooling pumps the fuel or oxidizer through passages surrounding the thrust chamber wall to absorb heat before injection.

name: Film cooling
description: Injecting a small portion of fuel or inert gas along the internal wall creates a protective film that shields the structure from high-temperature core gases.

name: Liquid rocket cycle
description: Liquid rocket engine cycles are classified into pressure-fed systems or pump-fed systems based on how propellants are pressurized.

name: Pump-fed cycle
description: A pump-fed open cycle where a fraction of the propellant is burned in a separate combustor to drive the turbine and is then exhausted overboard.

name: Gas-generator cycle
description: The gas generator must operate off-stoichiometric (extremely fuel-rich or oxidizer-rich) to prevent melting the turbine blades.

name: Staged combustion cycle
description: Because the turbine exhaust is injected into the main chamber rather than dumped at low pressure, it allows extremely high chamber pressures (P_c) and higher efficiency.

name: Turbopump power balance
description: In steady-state pump-fed cycles, the power produced by the turbine must equal the total mechanical power required to drive the oxidizer and fuel pumps.

name: Pump power requirement
description: The required shaft power for a propellant pump is proportional to the mass flow rate and pressure rise, divided by the pump efficiency (eta_p).

name: Real cycle analysis
description: Real engine cycle analysis incorporates component efficiencies, pressure losses, mechanical losses, and bleeding to predict realistic performance.

name: Real turbojet
description: The net thrust of a real turbojet must account for exit velocity variations caused by nozzle efficiency (eta_n) and incomplete expansion.

name: Real turbojet efficiency
description: Irreversibilities in the compressor and turbine increase entropy, directly decreasing the specific thrust and increasing the TSFC.

name: Turbine temperature ratio tau_t
description: In a real turbojet, the turbine temperature drop is determined by the actual power required to drive the compressor: tau_t = 1 - (tau_lambda / tau_r) * (tau_c - 1) / (eta_m * (1 + f)).

name: Fuel-air ratio f
description: The actual fuel-air ratio f accounts for combustor efficiency eta_b and variable specific heats across the burner.

name: Real afterburner
description: The afterburner burns remaining oxygen in the turbine exhaust gas, but its efficiency (eta_AB) is lower than the main combustor.

name: Real turbofan
description: Real turbofan cycle analysis must track the independent losses and state changes in both the core and the fan bypass duct.

name: Constant-pressure mixer
description: For proper aerodynamic mixing, the core and bypass streams must enter the mixer at substantially equal static pressures (P_5 = P_15).

name: Mixer efficiency
description: Aerodynamic mixing of streams with different total temperatures and velocities introduces viscous shearing losses, reducing overall total pressure.

name: Optimum fan pressure ratio
description: There is a distinct optimum fan pressure ratio (pi_f) that maximizes specific thrust or minimizes TSFC for a given bypass ratio and core technology.

name: Real turboprop
description: A real turboprop splits the available turbine energy into shaft power to drive the propeller and a small amount of jet thrust from the exhaust.

name: Propeller efficiency eta_prop
description: The efficiency with which the propeller converts the brake shaft horsepower into effective aircraft propulsive power.

name: Equivalent specific fuel consumption
description: For turboprops, ESFC (or S_e) combines the propeller shaft power and residual jet thrust into a single performance parameter.

name: Turbine expansion split
description: There is an optimum balance between how much expansion occurs in the turbine (for shaft power) versus the exhaust nozzle (for jet thrust) to maximize total equivalent thrust.

name: Off-design analysis
description: Engine performance analysis (or off-design analysis) predicts the performance of a specific engine across various flight conditions and throttle settings.

name: Fixed geometry
description: For a built engine, the physical throat areas of turbines and nozzles are geometrically fixed, which locks the aerodynamic coupling.

name: Corrected mass flow
description: Corrected mass flow rate m_dot_c is defined as m_dot * sqrt(theta) / delta, allowing data from different conditions to be collapsed onto a single curve.

name: Corrected speed
description: N_c = N / sqrt(theta). It relates the blade tip Mach number to the aerodynamic performance of turbomachinery.

name: Component matching
description: Steady-state off-design operation requires that the mass flow entering a component matches downstream constraints, and the turbine power balances the compressor power.

name: Choked turbine stator
description: If the high-pressure turbine nozzle guides are choked, the corrected mass flow exiting the compressor remains essentially constant, creating a fixed pumping constraint.

name: Compressor operating line
description: The steady-state compressor operating line on a compressor map is determined by the fixed throat area of the downstream turbine and exhaust nozzle.

name: Choked exhaust nozzle
description: When the convergent exhaust nozzle is choked, the operating pressure ratio across the turbine becomes independent of ambient pressure.

name: Control system
description: The fuel control unit (FCU) adjusts the fuel flow to match pilot thrust demands while keeping the engine within safety limits.

name: Engine limit
description: Mechanical stress restricts the maximum physical or corrected rotational speed of the fan spool.

name: Theta_break
description: Theta_break represents the ambient temperature point where the engine control transitions from limiting maximum compressor pressure ratio to limiting maximum turbine inlet temperature.

name: Cold day operation
description: At low ambient temperatures (below theta_break), the engine is typically limited by mechanical limits like pressure or spool speed.

name: Hot day operation
description: At high ambient temperatures (above theta_break), the engine control reduces fuel flow to protect the turbine from overheating, dropping the thrust.

name: Throttle hook
description: A throttle hook is a curve showing the relationship between thrust and thrust specific fuel consumption at a constant flight condition as the throttle is varied.

name: Transient operation
description: During acceleration, the turbine power must exceed the compressor power to accelerate the spool rotor inertia, causing the operating line to transiently swing toward the stall line.

name: Intermittent combustion

name: Mach number greater than one
description: Flow where the local Mach number is strictly greater than 1.0.

name: Mach number equal to one
description: Flow where the local Mach number is exactly equal to 1.0.

name: Total enthalpy of gas
description: Stagnation temperature (or total temperature) T_t represents the temperature achieved when a fluid is decelerated to zero velocity adiabatically.

name: Aerodynamic heating
description: The increase in temperature associated with deceleration of a high-speed flow is called aerodynamic heating.

name: Pressure at zero velocity isentropically
description: Stagnation pressure (or total pressure) P_t is the pressure attained when a fluid is brought to rest isentropically.

name: Constant entropy

name: Flow area variation with Mach number
description: The area-Mach number relation links the cross-sectional area of a duct to the local Mach number for an isentropic flow.

name: Convergent-divergent nozzle

name: Mass flow maximum limit
description: When the Mach number at the throat reaches unity, the mass flow rate through the nozzle reaches its maximum possible value and is said to be choked.

name: Discontinuity in supersonic flow
description: A normal shock wave is a thin discontinuity perpendicular to the flow direction that can occur only in supersonic flow.

name: Supersonic to Subsonic
description: The Mach number always drops from a supersonic value upstream to a subsonic value downstream of a normal shock.

name: Static pressure
description: Static pressure increases significantly across a normal shock wave.

name: Static temperature
description: Static temperature increases across a normal shock wave.

name: Total pressure
description: The total pressure decreases across a normal shock, which represents an irreversibility (entropy rise) in the flow.

name: Constant area flow with friction
description: Fanno flow refers to adiabatic flow in a constant-area duct with friction.

name: Unity
description: Friction always drives the Mach number toward unity in Fanno flow, whether the inlet flow is subsonic or supersonic.

name: Constant area flow with heat transfer
description: Rayleigh flow refers to frictionless flow in a constant-area duct with heat transfer (heating or cooling).

name: Maximum heat addition
description: Maximum heat addition in a Rayleigh flow occurs when the Mach number reaches unity; further heating causes thermal choking.

name: Momentum thrust and Pressure thrust
description: The total thrust of a rocket is the sum of the momentum thrust and the pressure thrust: F = m_dot * V_e + (P_e - P_a) * A_e.

name: Mass flow rate times Exhaust velocity
description: The component of thrust generated by the change in momentum of the exhaust gas (m_dot * V_e).

name: Pressure difference times Nozzle exit area
description: The component of thrust due to the difference between exit pressure and ambient pressure ((P_e - P_a) * A_e).

name: Thrust divided by Mass flow rate
description: The effective exhaust velocity C is defined such that F = m_dot * C, which combines momentum and pressure effects.

name: Thrust per unit weight flow rate
description: Specific impulse I_sp is the thrust divided by the propellant weight flow rate at sea level: I_sp = F / (m_dot * g_0).

name: Combustion chamber performance
description: The characteristic velocity c* is a measure of the combustion chemical energy and efficiency, independent of nozzle characteristics.

name: Chamber pressure and Throat area
description: c* = (P_c * A_t) / m_dot. It depends primarily on combustion temperature and molecular weight.

name: Nozzle expansion efficiency
description: The thrust coefficient C_f measures the amplification of thrust achieved by expanding the gas through the nozzle.

name: Thrust and Chamber pressure
description: C_f = F / (P_c * A_t). It is a function of the pressure ratio and area ratio of the nozzle.

name: Exit pressure equals Ambient pressure
description: Maximum thrust for a given propellant mass flow and chamber condition occurs when the nozzle exit pressure equals the ambient pressure (P_e = P_a).

name: Exit pressure less than Ambient pressure
description: A nozzle is overexpanded if the exit pressure is lower than the surrounding ambient atmospheric pressure.

name: Exit pressure greater than Ambient pressure
description: A nozzle is underexpanded if the gas exits at a pressure higher than the ambient atmospheric pressure.

name: Thrust decreasing with time

name: Empty structural mass

name: Payload mass to Initial mass
description: The ratio of the carried payload mass to the initial total mass of that specific rocket stage.

name: Determine performance trends
description: The objective of parametric cycle analysis is to relate the engine performance parameters to the design choices and the flight environment.

name: SAE Aerospace Standard
description: The gas turbine industry utilizes standard station numbering (e.g., 0 for ambient, 2 for compressor inlet, 3 for compressor exit, 4 for turbine inlet, 5 for turbine exit, 9 for nozzle exit).

name: Isentropic compression and expansion
description: Ideal cycle analysis assumes that the compression and expansion processes are reversible and adiabatic (isentropic).

name: Constant pressure combustion
description: It is assumed that combustion occurs at constant total pressure (no pressure drop in the combustor).

name: Fuel mass flow rate
description: The mass flow rate of fuel is neglected relative to the air mass flow rate in ideal performance matching (m_dot_f << m_dot_a).

name: Exit total temperature over Inlet total temperature
description: The dimensionless parameter tau represents the ratio of stagnation temperatures across a component.

name: Exit total pressure over Inlet total pressure
description: The dimensionless parameter pi represents the ratio of stagnation pressures across a component.

name: Pi equals tau to power of gamma over gamma-1
description: For ideal isentropic components (compressor or turbine), the total pressure ratio and total temperature ratio are directly coupled.

name: High Mach limit
description: For a given maximum turbine inlet temperature, the specific thrust of an ideal turbojet drops to zero at a specific upper flight Mach number limit.

name: Optimum compressor pressure ratio
description: For a fixed flight condition and turbine inlet temperature, there is an optimum compressor pressure ratio that maximizes the specific thrust of a turbojet.

name: Stagnation temperature at nozzle
description: An afterburner increases the total temperature of the gas entering the exhaust nozzle without affecting the turbomachinery core.

name: Core flow and Bypass flow
description: A turbofan engine divides the incoming air into a primary core stream and a secondary bypass stream.

name: Bypass mass flow divided by Core mass flow
description: alpha = m_dot_bypass / m_dot_core.

name: Turbomachinery
description: A ramjet engine has no compressor or turbine; compression is achieved entirely through the dynamic pressure rise in the inlet.

name: Zero static thrust
description: An ideal ramjet cannot produce any thrust at zero flight velocity (Mach = 0) because it lacks a mechanical compressor.

name: Bypass and Core exit velocities to be equal
description: For an unmixed ideal turbofan, the optimum kinetic energy distribution occurs when the exit velocity of the bypass nozzle equals the exit velocity of the core nozzle.

name: Component efficiencies and Total pressure ratios
description: The performance of real components is characterized by total temperature ratios, total pressure ratios, efficiencies, and pressure losses.

name: Total pressure ratio pi_d
description: The performance of the inlet (or diffuser) is primarily characterized by its total pressure ratio, pi_d = P_t2 / P_t0, also called the inlet recovery factor.

name: Flight Mach number
description: Military specifications (like MIL-E-5007D) define standard inlet recovery curves that decrease as the flight Mach number increases above 1.0.

name: Capture area air mass flow to Maximum air mass flow
description: The ratio of the actual mass flow entered into the inlet to the maximum possible mass flow that the capture area can intercept.

name: Isentropic efficiency eta_c
description: The isentropic compressor efficiency eta_c is defined as the ratio of ideal (isentropic) work to the actual work required for a given total pressure ratio.

name: Isentropic efficiency and Total pressure ratio
description: tau_c = 1 + (pi_c^((gamma-1)/gamma) - 1) / eta_c, which links actual temperature rise to pressure ratio.

name: Isentropic efficiency of an infinitesimal stage
description: Polytropic efficiency (e_c for compressor, e_t for turbine) is defined as the isentropic efficiency of an elemental or infinitesimal stage.

name: Increasing pressure ratio
description: For a constant polytropic efficiency e_c, the overall isentropic compressor efficiency eta_c drops as the total pressure ratio pi_c increases due to the preheating effect.

name: Isentropic efficiency eta_t
description: The isentropic turbine efficiency eta_t is defined as the ratio of actual work output to the ideal (isentropic) work output for a given total pressure ratio.

name: Combustion efficiency eta_b
description: Combustion efficiency eta_b is the ratio of the actual thermal energy released to the chemical energy available in the fuel.

name: Total pressure ratio pi_b
description: The total pressure ratio of the combustor pi_b = P_t4 / P_t3 is always less than 1.0 due to viscous friction and cold-to-hot flow momentum pressure drop.

name: Friction and Fundamental thermal loading
description: Total pressure drops because of skin friction in the liner liners/swirlers and the fundamental thermodynamic loss from adding heat at finite Mach numbers.

name: Afterburner efficiency eta_AB
description: The efficiency eta_AB measures how completely the fuel burns in the afterburner duct upstream of the exit nozzle.

name: Total pressure ratio pi_AB
description: The total pressure ratio pi_AB = P_t7 / P_t6 account for losses due to flameholders, friction, and high-temperature heat addition.

name: Mechanical efficiency eta_m
description: Mechanical efficiency eta_m accounts for frictional power losses in bearings and accessory gearboxes connecting the turbine and compressor shafts.

name: Total pressure ratio pi_n
description: The exhaust nozzle performance is characterized by its total pressure ratio pi_n = P_t9 / P_t7, which represents friction losses in the nozzle duct.

name: Exit momentum thrust
description: An angularity factor (or divergence factor C_ang) accounts for the non-axial exit velocity vector at the nozzle plane, reducing net thrust.

name: Available turbine power for compression
description: Extraction of mechanical shaft power (P_TO) to run aircraft accessories directly reduces the turbine power available to drive the compressor.

name: Core mass flow rate
description: Extracting high-pressure compressed air from the compressor exit for cabin environmental control systems (ECS) or turbine blade cooling reduces the downstream mass flow.

name: Turbine inlet stagnation temperature
description: Reintroducing relatively cool bleed air into the turbine stages for blade cooling causes aerodynamic mixing losses and lowers the effective total temperature of the gas.

name: Component efficiencies and Chemical reactions
description: Analysis of real rocket engines requires accounting for non-ideal effects including nozzle efficiency, incomplete combustion, heat transfer, and complex chemical behaviors.

name: Stagnation pressure at throat
description: Due to high-velocity combustion and friction inside the chamber, the total pressure drops from the injector head to the nozzle throat entrance.

name: Nozzle efficiency eta_n
description: Nozzle efficiency eta_n is defined as the ratio of actual kinetic energy change to the ideal isentropic kinetic energy change across the nozzle.

name: Actual exit velocity divided by Isentropic velocity
description: The velocity coefficient C_v relates the actual exhaust velocity to the ideal velocity; typically C_v equals the square root of nozzle efficiency.

name: Mass flow rate deviation
description: The discharge coefficient C_d is the ratio of actual mass flow rate to the ideal isentropic mass flow rate, accounting for boundary layer displacement.

name: Chamber stagnation temperature
description: Failure to achieve perfect chemical equilibrium or full mixing of oxidizer and fuel lowers the combustion temperature T_c below its theoretical adiabatic value.

name: Characteristic velocity ratio
description: Combustion efficiency is often expressed as the ratio of actual characteristic velocity (c*_actual) to the theoretical characteristic velocity (c*_theoretical).

name: Fixed chemical composition
description: Frozen flow assumes that the chemical composition of the exhaust gas remains constant (fixed at chamber exit state) during expansion through the nozzle.

name: Instantaneous chemical reaction
description: Equilibrium flow assumes that chemical reactions occur instantaneously as pressure and temperature drop, continually adjusting composition to maintain local equilibrium.

name: Higher specific impulse
description: Equilibrium flow gives higher calculated exhaust velocity and specific impulse than frozen flow because chemical recombination energy is recovered as kinetic energy.

name: Frozen flow and Equilibrium flow limits
description: The actual expansion process in a real rocket nozzle falls between the ideal frozen and shifting equilibrium bounds.

name: Exhaust gas enthalpy
description: Heat loss through the chamber walls and nozzle liners directly reduces the thermal energy available for conversion into kinetic energy.

name: Fuel through cooling jackets
description: Regenerative cooling pumps the fuel or oxidizer through passages surrounding the thrust chamber wall to absorb heat before injection.

name: Wall heat loss
description: The heat absorbed by the coolant is reintroduced into the combustion chamber, preventing a net thermodynamic energy loss.

name: Cooling fluid boundary layer
description: Injecting a small portion of fuel or inert gas along the internal wall creates a protective film that shields the structure from high-temperature core gases.

name: Pressure-fed cycle
description: Liquid rocket engine cycles are classified into pressure-fed systems or pump-fed systems based on how propellants are pressurized.

name: Expander cycle
description: A closed cycle where fuel is vaporized in the cooling jacket and then routes directly through the turbine to drive the pumps before entering the injector.

name: Turbine inlet temperature
description: The gas generator must operate off-stoichiometric (extremely fuel-rich or oxidizer-rich) to prevent melting the turbine blades.

name: Higher chamber pressure
description: Because the turbine exhaust is injected into the main chamber rather than dumped at low pressure, it allows extremely high chamber pressures (P_c) and higher efficiency.

name: Turbine power equals Pump power
description: In steady-state pump-fed cycles, the power produced by the turbine must equal the total mechanical power required to drive the oxidizer and fuel pumps.

name: Volumetric flow rate and Pressure rise
description: The required shaft power for a propellant pump is proportional to the mass flow rate and pressure rise, divided by the pump efficiency (eta_p).

name: Component efficiencies and fluid losses
description: Real engine cycle analysis incorporates component efficiencies, pressure losses, mechanical losses, and bleeding to predict realistic performance.

name: Viscous and shock losses
description: In real engines, component total pressure ratios (like pi_d, pi_b, pi_n) are less than 1.0 due to friction and shock waves.

name: Real exit velocity and pressure
description: The net thrust of a real turbojet must account for exit velocity variations caused by nozzle efficiency (eta_n) and incomplete expansion.

name: Component irreversibilities
description: Irreversibilities in the compressor and turbine increase entropy, directly decreasing the specific thrust and increasing the TSFC.

name: Compressor power balance
description: In a real turbojet, the turbine temperature drop is determined by the actual power required to drive the compressor: tau_t = 1 - (tau_lambda / tau_r) * (tau_c - 1) / (eta_m * (1 + f)).

name: Combustor energy balance
description: The actual fuel-air ratio f accounts for combustor efficiency eta_b and variable specific heats across the burner.

name: Additional fuel injection
description: The afterburner burns remaining oxygen in the turbine exhaust gas, but its efficiency (eta_AB) is lower than the main combustor.

name: High total pressure drop
description: Adding heat at a finite Mach number inside the afterburner duct causes a fundamental thermal total pressure drop (Rayleigh effect).

name: Core stream and Bypass stream
description: Real turbofan cycle analysis must track the independent losses and state changes in both the core and the fan bypass duct.

name: Unmixed turbofan
description: An engine configuration where the core and bypass streams exhaust through separate independent nozzles.

name: Mixed-flow turbofan
description: An engine configuration where the core and bypass streams mix in a common mixer component before expanding through a single nozzle.

name: Equal static pressures at inlet
description: For proper aerodynamic mixing, the core and bypass streams must enter the mixer at substantially equal static pressures (P_5 = P_15).

name: Total pressure gain or loss
description: Aerodynamic mixing of streams with different total temperatures and velocities introduces viscous shearing losses, reducing overall total pressure.

name: Component efficiencies
description: Lower component efficiencies (like lower fan or turbine efficiency) shift the optimum bypass ratio (alpha) toward lower values compared to ideal cycles.

name: Specific thrust of turbofan
description: There is a distinct optimum fan pressure ratio (pi_f) that maximizes specific thrust or minimizes TSFC for a given bypass ratio and core technology.

name: Shaft power and Residual thrust
description: A real turboprop splits the available turbine energy into shaft power to drive the propeller and a small amount of jet thrust from the exhaust.

name: Shaft power conversion to thrust
description: The efficiency with which the propeller converts the brake shaft horsepower into effective aircraft propulsive power.

name: Fuel flow divided by Equivalent thrust
description: For turboprops, ESFC (or S_e) combines the propeller shaft power and residual jet thrust into a single performance parameter.

name: Optimum nozzle pressure ratio
description: There is an optimum balance between how much expansion occurs in the turbine (for shaft power) versus the exhaust nozzle (for jet thrust) to maximize total equivalent thrust.

name: Required turbine temperature drop
description: Extracting mechanical power from the shaft forces the turbine to work harder, which reduces the total enthalpy available for the exhaust jet.

name: Predict performance of a fixed engine
description: Engine performance analysis (or off-design analysis) predicts the performance of a specific engine across various flight conditions and throttle settings.

name: Component flow areas
description: For a built engine, the physical throat areas of turbines and nozzles are geometrically fixed, which locks the aerodynamic coupling.

name: Mass flow scaled by dimensionless temperature and pressure
description: Corrected mass flow rate m_dot_c is defined as m_dot * sqrt(theta) / delta, allowing data from different conditions to be collapsed onto a single curve.

name: Physical rotational speed divided by square root of theta
description: N_c = N / sqrt(theta). It relates the blade tip Mach number to the aerodynamic performance of turbomachinery.

name: Continuity of mass and power balance
description: Steady-state off-design operation requires that the mass flow entering a component matches downstream constraints, and the turbine power balances the compressor power.

name: Upstream compressor operating point
description: If the high-pressure turbine nozzle guides are choked, the corrected mass flow exiting the compressor remains essentially constant, creating a fixed pumping constraint.

name: Turbine flow capacity
description: The steady-state compressor operating line on a compressor map is determined by the fixed throat area of the downstream turbine and exhaust nozzle.

name: Turbine pressure ratio
description: When the convergent exhaust nozzle is choked, the operating pressure ratio across the turbine becomes independent of ambient pressure.

name: Fuel flow rate and variable geometry
description: The fuel control unit (FCU) adjusts the fuel flow to match pilot thrust demands while keeping the engine within safety limits.

name: Maximum fan speed
description: Mechanical stress restricts the maximum physical or corrected rotational speed of the fan spool.

name: Maximum compressor discharge pressure
description: Structural casing design restricts the maximum compressor exit pressure (P_t3) to prevent burst failure.

name: Maximum turbine inlet temperature
description: Material thermal properties restrict the maximum allowable gas temperature entering the turbine blades (T_t4).

name: Control logic transition point
description: Theta_break represents the ambient temperature point where the engine control transitions from limiting maximum compressor pressure ratio to limiting maximum turbine inlet temperature.

name: Maximum pressure or shaft speed
description: At low ambient temperatures (below theta_break), the engine is typically limited by mechanical limits like pressure or spool speed.

name: Thrust versus TSFC
description: A throttle hook is a curve showing the relationship between thrust and thrust specific fuel consumption at a constant flight condition as the throttle is varied.

name: Temporary power imbalance
description: During acceleration, the turbine power must exceed the compressor power to accelerate the spool rotor inertia, causing the operating line to transiently swing toward the stall line.

name: Ideal Brayton cycle
description: The realistic engine cycle analysis (Chapter 7) modifies the ideal Brayton cycle (Chapter 4) by incorporating polytropic efficiencies and pressure drops (Chapter 5).

name: Nozzle throat area
description: The physical throat area of the components designed in Chapters 4 and 7 acts as a geometric constraint that fixes the operating line in Chapter 8.

name: Design point parameters
description: Reference design choices (Chapters 4 & 7) define the fixed constants (like turbine area) needed for off-design performance evaluation (Chapter 8).

name: Isentropic flow theory
description: Isentropic area-Mach relations from Chapter 2 are directly utilized to design rocket nozzles in Chapter 3 and exhaust nozzles in Chapters 4 and 5.

name: Normal shock wave
description: The total pressure drop across a normal shock (Chapter 2) explains the reduction of inlet recovery pi_d in supersonic flight (Chapters 5 and 7).

name: Choked flow condition
description: The throat choking criterion (Chapter 2) becomes the fundamental law regulating component mass flow matching in off-design operation (Chapter 8).

name: Propellant mass flow
description: The design propellant mass flow derived from Chapter 3 specific impulse requirements must satisfy the pump-turbine shaft power matching in Chapter 6.

name: Turbine material thermal limit
description: The metallurgical temperature limit of turbine blades (Chapter 5) establishes the boundary for the hot-day Theta_break control logic (Chapter 8).

name: Afterburner pressure drop
description: The fundamental thermal pressure drop in afterburners (Chapter 5 Rayleigh effect) severely penalizes the real augmented TSFC calculated in Chapter 7.

name: Off-design performance
description: Reference design choices (Chapters 4 & 7) define the fixed constants (like turbine area) needed for off-design performance evaluation (Chapter 8).

name: Real supersonic inlet
description: The total pressure drop across a normal shock (Chapter 2) explains the reduction of inlet recovery pi_d in supersonic flight (Chapters 5 and 7).

name: Maximum combustor heat addition
description: The foundational physics of Rayleigh flow and thermal choking (Chapter 2) constraint the maximum fuel injection in burners (Chapters 5, 7, and 8).

name: Mass flow alignment
description: The throat choking criterion (Chapter 2) becomes the fundamental law regulating component mass flow matching in off-design operation (Chapter 8).

name: Nozzle efficiency and chemical kinetics
description: The ideal rocket thrust relations (Chapter 3) are modified in Chapter 6 by implementing nozzle velocity coefficients and shifting/frozen chemical behaviors.

name: Optimal engine bypass ratio
description: The combustor and duct pressure losses detailed in Chapter 5 directly reduce the theoretical optimum bypass ratio when evaluated in Chapter 7 real cycles.

name: Component temperature ratios
description: The stage-independent polytropic efficiencies defined in Chapter 5 are used as fundamental inputs for real cycle (Chapter 7) and off-design (Chapter 8) math models.

name: Control logic shift to Theta_break
description: The metallurgical temperature limit of turbine blades (Chapter 5) establishes the boundary for the hot-day Theta_break control logic (Chapter 8).
